NASB.1: And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, 'Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.
NASB.2: 'The fear of you and the terror of you will be on every beast of the earth and on every bird of the sky; with everything that creeps on the ground, and all the fish of the sea, into your hand they are given.
NASB.3: 'Every moving thing that is alive shall be food for you; I give all to you, as [I gave] the green plant.
NASB.4: 'Only you shall not eat flesh with its life, [that is], its blood.
NASB.5: 'Surely I will require your lifeblood; from every beast I will require it. And from [every] man, from every man's brother I will require the life of man.
NASB.6: 'Whoever sheds man's blood, By man his blood shall be shed, For in the image of God He made man.
NASB.7: 'As for you, be fruitful and multiply; Populate the earth abundantly and multiply in it.'
NASB.8: Then God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying,
NASB.9: 'Now behold, I Myself do establish My covenant with you, and with your descendants after you;
NASB.10: and with every living creature that is with you, the birds, the cattle, and every beast of the earth with you; of all that comes out of the ark, even every beast of the earth.
NASB.11: 'I establish My covenant with you; and all flesh shall never again be cut off by the water of the flood, neither shall there again be a flood to destroy the earth.'
NASB.12: God said, 'This is the sign of the covenant which I am making between Me and you and every living creature that is with you, for all successive generations;
NASB.13: I set My bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of a covenant between Me and the earth.
NASB.14: 'It shall come about, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow will be seen in the cloud,
NASB.15: and I will remember My covenant, which is between Me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and never again shall the water become a flood to destroy all flesh.
NASB.16: 'When the bow is in the cloud, then I will look upon it, to remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.'
NASB.17: And God said to Noah, 'This is the sign of the covenant which I have established between Me and all flesh that is on the earth.'
NASB.18: Now the sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem and Ham and Japheth; and Ham was the father of Canaan.
NASB.19: These three [were] the sons of Noah, and from these the whole earth was populated.
NASB.20: Then Noah began farming and planted a vineyard.
NASB.21: He drank of the wine and became drunk, and uncovered himself inside his tent.
NASB.22: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside.
NASB.23: But Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it upon both their shoulders and walked backward and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were turned away, so that they did not see their father's nakedness.
NASB.24: When Noah awoke from his wine, he knew what his youngest son had done to him.
NASB.25: So he said, 'Cursed be Canaan; A servant of servants He shall be to his brothers.'
NASB.26: He also said, 'Blessed be the LORD, The God of Shem; And let Canaan be his servant.
NASB.27: 'May God enlarge Japheth, And let him dwell in the tents of Shem; And let Canaan be his servant.'
NASB.28: Noah lived three hundred and fifty years after the flood.
NASB.29: So all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.

ESV.1: And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.
ESV.2: The fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth and upon every bird of the heavens, upon everything that creeps on the ground and all the fish of the sea. Into your hand they are delivered.
ESV.3: Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you. And as I gave you the green plants, I give you everything.
ESV.4: But you shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood.
ESV.5: And for your lifeblood I will require a reckoning: from every beast I will require it and from man. From his fellow man I will require a reckoning for the life of man.
ESV.6: “Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed, for God made man in his own image.
ESV.7: And you,  be fruitful and multiply, increase greatly on the earth and multiply in it.”
ESV.8: Then God said to Noah and to his sons with him,
ESV.9: “Behold, I establish my covenant with you and your offspring after you,
ESV.10: and with every living creature that is with you, the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth with you, as many as came out of the ark; it is for every beast of the earth.
ESV.11: I establish my covenant with you, that never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, and never again shall there be a flood to destroy the earth.”
ESV.12: And God said, “This is the sign of the covenant that I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for all future generations:
ESV.13: I have set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
ESV.14: When I bring clouds over the earth and the bow is seen in the clouds,
ESV.15: I will remember my covenant that is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh. And the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
ESV.16: When the bow is in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”
ESV.17: God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between me and all flesh that is on the earth.”
ESV.18: The sons of Noah who went forth from the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. (Ham was the father of Canaan.)
ESV.19: These three were the sons of Noah, and from these the people of the whole earth were dispersed.
ESV.20: Noah began to be a man of the soil, and he planted a vineyard.
ESV.21: He drank of the wine and became drunk and lay uncovered in his tent.
ESV.22: And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father and told his two brothers outside.
ESV.23: Then Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it on both their shoulders, and walked backward and covered the nakedness of their father. Their faces were turned backward, and they did not see their father's nakedness.
ESV.24: When Noah awoke from his wine and knew what his youngest son had done to him,
ESV.25: he said, “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be to his brothers.”
ESV.26: He also said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem; and let Canaan be his servant.
ESV.27: May God enlarge Japheth,  and let him dwell in the tents of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant.”
ESV.28: After the flood Noah lived 350 years.
ESV.29: All the days of Noah were 950 years, and he died.

NLT.1: Then God blessed Noah and his sons and told them, “Be fruitful and multiply. Fill the earth.
NLT.2: All the animals of the earth, all the birds of the sky, all the small animals that scurry along the ground, and all the fish in the sea will look on you with fear and terror. I have placed them in your power.
NLT.3: I have given them to you for food, just as I have given you grain and vegetables.
NLT.4: But you must never eat any meat that still has the lifeblood in it.
NLT.5: “And I will require the blood of anyone who takes another person’s life. If a wild animal kills a person, it must die. And anyone who murders a fellow human must die.
NLT.6: If anyone takes a human life, that person’s life will also be taken by human hands. For God made human beings in his own image.
NLT.7: Now be fruitful and multiply, and repopulate the earth.”
NLT.8: Then God told Noah and his sons,
NLT.9: “I hereby confirm my covenant with you and your descendants,
NLT.10: and with all the animals that were on the boat with you — the birds, the livestock, and all the wild animals — every living creature on earth.
NLT.11: Yes, I am confirming my covenant with you. Never again will floodwaters kill all living creatures; never again will a flood destroy the earth.”
NLT.12: Then God said, “I am giving you a sign of my covenant with you and with all living creatures, for all generations to come.
NLT.13: I have placed my rainbow in the clouds. It is the sign of my covenant with you and with all the earth.
NLT.14: When I send clouds over the earth, the rainbow will appear in the clouds,
NLT.15: and I will remember my covenant with you and with all living creatures. Never again will the floodwaters destroy all life.
NLT.16: When I see the rainbow in the clouds, I will remember the eternal covenant between God and every living creature on earth.”
NLT.17: Then God said to Noah, “Yes, this rainbow is the sign of the covenant I am confirming with all the creatures on earth.”
NLT.18: The sons of Noah who came out of the boat with their father were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. (Ham is the father of Canaan.)
NLT.19: From these three sons of Noah came all the people who now populate the earth.
NLT.20: After the flood, Noah began to cultivate the ground, and he planted a vineyard.
NLT.21: One day he drank some wine he had made, and he became drunk and lay naked inside his tent.
NLT.22: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw that his father was naked and went outside and told his brothers.
NLT.23: Then Shem and Japheth took a robe, held it over their shoulders, and backed into the tent to cover their father. As they did this, they looked the other way so they would not see him naked.
NLT.24: When Noah woke up from his stupor, he learned what Ham, his youngest son, had done.
NLT.25:
Then he cursed Canaan, the son of Ham: “May Canaan be cursed!
May he be the lowest of servants to his relatives.”
NLT.26:
Then Noah said, “May the LORD, the God of Shem, be blessed,
and may Canaan be his servant!
NLT.27:
May God expand the territory of Japheth!
May Japheth share the prosperity of Shem,
and may Canaan be his servant.”
NLT.28: Noah lived another 350 years after the great flood.
NLT.29: He lived 950 years, and then he died.

WEB.1: God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth.
WEB.2: The fear of you and the dread of you will be on every animal of the earth, and on every bird of the sky. Everything that moves along the ground, and all the fish of the sea, are delivered into your hand.
WEB.3: Every moving thing that lives will be food for you. As I gave you the green herb, I have given everything to you.
WEB.4: But flesh with its life, that is, its blood, you shall not eat.
WEB.5: I will surely require your blood of your lives; at the hand of every animal I will require it. At the hand of man, even at the hand of every man’s brother, I will require the life of man.
WEB.6: Whoever sheds man’s blood, his blood will be shed by man, for God made man in his own image.
WEB.7: Be fruitful and multiply. Increase abundantly in the earth, and multiply in it.”
WEB.8: God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying,
WEB.9: “As for me, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your offspring after you,
WEB.10: and with every living creature that is with you: the birds, the livestock, and every animal of the earth with you, of all that go out of the ship, even every animal of the earth.
WEB.11: I will establish my covenant with you: All flesh will not be cut off any more by the waters of the flood. There will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”
WEB.12: God said, “This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
WEB.13: I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.
WEB.14: When I bring a cloud over the earth, that the rainbow will be seen in the cloud,
WEB.15: and I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the waters will no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
WEB.16: The rainbow will be in the cloud. I will look at it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”
WEB.17: God said to Noah, “This is the token of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is on the earth.”
WEB.18: The sons of Noah who went out from the ship were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham is the father of Canaan.
WEB.19: These three were the sons of Noah, and from these, the whole earth was populated.
WEB.20: Noah began to be a farmer, and planted a vineyard.
WEB.21: He drank of the wine and got drunk. He was uncovered within his tent.
WEB.22: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside.
WEB.23: Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it on both their shoulders, went in backwards, and covered the nakedness of their father. Their faces were backwards, and they didn’t see their father’s nakedness.
WEB.24: Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done to him.
WEB.25: He said, “Canaan is cursed. He will be a servant of servants to his brothers.”
WEB.26: He said, “Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Shem. Let Canaan be his servant.
WEB.27: May God enlarge Japheth. Let him dwell in the tents of Shem. Let Canaan be his servant.”
WEB.28: Noah lived three hundred fifty years after the flood.
WEB.29: All the days of Noah were nine hundred fifty years, and then he died.

CSB17.1: God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.2: The fear and terror of you will be in every living creature on the earth, every bird of the sky, every creature that crawls on the ground, and all the fish of the sea. They are placed under your authority. <sup>[1]</sup>
CSB17.3: Every creature that lives and moves will be food for you; <sup>ⓐ</sup> as I gave the green plants, I have given you everything. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.4: However, you must not eat meat with its lifeblood in it. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.5: And I will require a penalty for your lifeblood; <sup>[2]</sup> I will require it from any animal <sup>ⓓ</sup> and from any human; if someone murders a fellow human, I will require that person’s life. <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.6:
Whoever sheds human blood,
by humans his blood will be shed, ⓕ
for God made humans in his image. ⓖ
CSB17.7: But you, be fruitful and multiply; spread out over the earth and multiply on it.” <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.8: Then God said to Noah and his sons with him,
CSB17.9: “Understand that I am establishing my covenant <sup>ⓘ</sup> with you and your descendants after you,

AMP.1: And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.
AMP.2: The fear and the terror of you shall be [instinctive] in every animal of the land and in every bird of the air; and together with everything that moves on the ground, and with all the fish of the sea; they are given into your hand.
AMP.3: Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you; I give you everything, as I gave you the green plants and vegetables.
AMP.4: But you shall not eat meat along with its life, that is, its blood.
AMP.5: For your lifeblood I will most certainly require an accounting; from every animal [that kills a person] I will require it. And from man, from every man's brother [that is, anyone who murders] I will require the life of man.
AMP.6:
"Whoever sheds man's blood [unlawfully],
By man (judicial government) shall his blood be shed,
For in the image of God
He made man.
AMP.7:
"As for you, be fruitful and multiply;
Populate the earth abundantly and multiply in it."
AMP.8: Then God spoke to Noah and to his sons with him, saying,
AMP.9: "Now behold, I am establishing My covenant (binding agreement, solemn promise) with you and with your descendants after you
AMP.10: and with every living creature that is with you—the birds, the livestock, and the wild animals of the earth along with you, of everything that comes out of the ark—every living creature of the earth.
AMP.11: I will establish My covenant with you: Never again shall all flesh be cut off by the water of a flood, nor shall there ever again be a flood to destroy and ruin the earth."
AMP.12: And God said, "This is the token (visible symbol, memorial) of the [solemn] covenant which I am making between Me and you and every living creature that is with you, for all future generations;
AMP.13: I set My rainbow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of a covenant between Me and the earth.
AMP.14: It shall come about, when I bring clouds over the earth, that the rainbow shall be seen in the clouds,
AMP.15: and I will [compassionately] remember My covenant, which is between Me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and never again will the water become a flood to destroy all flesh.
AMP.16: When the rainbow is in the clouds and I look at it, I will [solemnly] remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth."
AMP.17: And God said to Noah, "This [rainbow] is the sign of the covenant (solemn pledge, binding agreement) which I have established between Me and all living things on the earth."
AMP.18: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem and Ham and Japheth. Ham would become the father of Canaan.
AMP.19: These are the three sons of Noah, and from these [men] the whole earth was populated and scattered with inhabitants.
AMP.20: And Noah began to farm and cultivate the ground and he planted a vineyard.
AMP.21: He drank some of the wine and became drunk, and he was uncovered and lay exposed inside his tent.
AMP.22: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw [by accident] the nakedness of his father, and [to his father's shame] told his two brothers outside.
AMP.23: So Shem and Japheth took a robe and put it on both their shoulders, and walked backwards and covered the nakedness of their father; their faces were turned away so that they did not see their father's nakedness.
AMP.24: When Noah awoke from his wine [induced stupor], he knew what his younger son [Ham] had done to him.
AMP.25:
So he said,
"Cursed be Canaan [the son of Ham];
A servant of servants
He shall be to his brothers."
AMP.26:
He also said,
"Blessed be the LORD,
The God of Shem;
And let Canaan be his servant.
AMP.27:
"May God enlarge [the land of] Japheth,
And let him dwell in the tents of Shem;
And let Canaan be his servant."
AMP.28: Noah lived three hundred and fifty years after the flood.
AMP.29: So all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.
